lessons.title: Paragraph main idea
lessons.objective: Read a paragraph and pick its main idea.

introduce.text: The main idea is what a whole paragraph is mostly about. Think of it as the big message in one short sentence.
introduce.speech: The main idea is what a whole paragraph is mostly about. Think of it as the big message in one short sentence.

introduce.text: The other sentences are details. Details give facts that support the main idea, like pillars holding up a roof.
introduce.speech: The other sentences are details. Details give facts that support the main idea, like pillars holding up a roof.

demonstrate.text: Read: Ravi's cow gives milk. The milk is sold in the village. Ravi's family earns money from it. Main idea: the cow helps Ravi's family earn money.
demonstrate.speech: Read: Ravi's cow gives milk. The milk is sold in the village. Ravi's family earns money from it. Main idea: the cow helps Ravi's family earn money.

demonstrate.text: Test your idea: do ALL the sentences fit it? A sentence that is only a small fact is a detail, not the main idea.
demonstrate.speech: Test your idea: do ALL the sentences fit it? A sentence that is only a small fact is a detail, not the main idea.

guided.prompt: Rani's family grows tomatoes, chillies and brinjals on their roof. They water the pots daily and eat the vegetables fresh. What is the main idea?
guided.speech: Rani's family grows tomatoes, chillies and brinjals on their roof. They water the pots daily and eat the vegetables fresh. What is the main idea?
options: Rani's family grows vegetables on their roof
guided.answer: Rani's family grows vegetables on their roof
hints: Ask: what do ALL the sentences talk about, not just one of them?
Tomatoes, chillies and watering pots all point to growing vegetables on the roof.

wrong_feedback.Tomatoes are red: Tomatoes are only one small detail. The whole paragraph is about more than that.
wrong_feedback.Rani cooks dinner each night: The paragraph never says anything about cooking dinner.

guided.explanation: Every sentence is about growing vegetables on the roof.

guided.prompt: Our school ground is busy at lunch. Some children play kabaddi, some skip, and others run races. What is the main idea?
guided.speech: Our school ground is busy at lunch. Some children play kabaddi, some skip, and others run races. What is the main idea?
options: Skipping ropes are made of cotton
The school ground is very small
Children play many games at lunch
guided.answer: Children play many games at lunch
hints: Which choice covers kabaddi, skipping and races together?
Kabaddi, skipping and races are all games children play.

wrong_feedback.Skipping ropes are made of cotton: Nothing is said about what ropes are made of, and it is a tiny detail.
wrong_feedback.The school ground is very small: The paragraph never mentions the size of the ground.

guided.explanation: Kabaddi, skipping and races are all games played at lunch.

lessons.title: Context clues
lessons.objective: Work out the meaning of a new word from the sentence around it.

introduce.text: Context clues are the words around a hard word. They give hints about what it means.
introduce.speech: Context clues are the words around a hard word. They give hints about what it means.

introduce.text: Read the whole sentence, and the one before or after. Then ask: what meaning would make sense here?
introduce.speech: Read the whole sentence, and the one before or after. Then ask: what meaning would make sense here?

demonstrate.text: Sometimes the clue is an opposite: The road was smooth, not bumpy. 'Not bumpy' tells us smooth means even, with no bumps.

lessons.title: Prefixes and suffixes

introduce.text: A prefix is a small part added to the START of a word. It changes the meaning. un- means not, and re- means again.

introduce.text: A suffix is a small part added to the END of a word. -ful means full of, and -less means without.

demonstrate.text: un- + kind = unkind, which means not kind. re- + read = reread, which means read again.

demonstrate.text: care + ful = careful, which means full of care. care + less = careless, which means without care.

lessons.title: Parts of speech
